notes: Playtester persona bank. Use breaks_on and review_questions when simulating a persona; keep adding personas that match your actual players, not your imaginary audience.

personas.label: Never Played Anything
likes: being told what to do next
table_behaviours: asks 'what do I do now?' often
play_goals: wants to feel competent fast
likely_failure_modes: drops core rules mid-game
plays by vibe
red_flags_to_watch: first turn needs more than one decision
win condition not visible on the table
breaks_on: rules that only make sense after reading a later section
review_questions: Could they take their first turn from the player aid alone?
Do they know how to win by the end of the teach?
personas.sample_quote: Sorry, what am I trying to do again?
personas.use_when: Always, for any game that claims to be teachable or family-weight.

personas.label: Basic Board Gamer
play_goals: wants a smooth evening
likely_failure_modes: skips upkeep steps
misses card effects printed below the fold
red_flags_to_watch: upkeep phase with more than three steps
breaks_on: conditional text at the bottom of a card
review_questions: What happens if they forget the upkeep step entirely? Does anyone notice?
Is the important card text in the first line?
personas.sample_quote: Oh, was I meant to do something at the end of the round?
personas.use_when: Light and mid-weight games aimed at the general hobby market.

personas.label: Party Game Regular
play_goals: wants energy to stay high
likely_failure_modes: house-rules away anything slow
misses quiet scoring conditions
red_flags_to_watch: rules that must be read aloud mid-game
breaks_on: simultaneous secret planning with no timer
review_questions: Where does the table go silent for more than a minute?
Which rule will they drop first to keep the energy up?
personas.sample_quote: Can we just say it does that and keep going?
personas.use_when: Party, social and light filler games, and any game pitched as 'fun with friends'.

personas.label: Gateway Euro Convert
play_goals: wants meaningful choices
likely_failure_modes: over-trusts examples that don't cover their case
paralysed by an unclear end trigger
red_flags_to_watch: end trigger not stated in one place
breaks_on: iconography that changes meaning by context
take-that cards in an otherwise peaceful engine game
review_questions: Can they say exactly when the game ends?
Does any icon mean two different things?
personas.sample_quote: Is there a worked example of this? I want to make sure I'm doing it right.
personas.use_when: Mid-weight euros and engine builders aimed at players moving up from gateway games.

personas.label: Heavy Euro Planner
play_goals: wants skill to matter
likely_failure_modes: analysis paralysis slows the whole table
finds the optimal line and stops exploring
breaks_on: actions whose value is unclear until later
review_questions: Is there a free or cheap action they can chain indefinitely?
How long is their worst turn, and is that the game's fault?
personas.sample_quote: Hang on, let me count this out again.
personas.use_when: Heavy euros, worker placement, and anything with a tight action economy.

personas.label: 18xx Shark
play_goals: wants brutal clarity
likely_failure_modes: exploits soft money rules
dominates auctions against weaker players
review_questions: What happens when the bank runs out mid-payout?
Who wins a tied bid?
personas.sample_quote: Does the dividend pay before or after the price moves? It matters.
personas.use_when: Economic, stock, auction and route-building games.

personas.label: 18xx Learner With Teeth
play_goals: wants training wheels without shame
likely_failure_modes: stalls on an unclear private company or special power
assumes examples are exhaustive
red_flags_to_watch: special powers explained only on the component
breaks_on: special-case components with no rulebook entry
review_questions: Is every special power explained somewhere they can look it up?
Does each example show every step?
personas.sample_quote: I think I've got it, but can you check my maths?
personas.use_when: Deep economic games with a learning curve; checks whether the teach scales.

personas.label: 4X Diplomat
play_goals: wants politics to matter
likely_failure_modes: turns the game into a negotiation sim the rules don't support
unenforceable deals cause rows
red_flags_to_watch: no rule on whether deals are binding
breaks_on: silence on binding vs non-binding deals
hidden information that can be 'shown' to an ally
review_questions: Are deals binding? Does the rulebook say so?
Can they show their hand to an ally?
personas.sample_quote: Let's make a deal: I leave your border alone for two turns.
personas.use_when: Multiplayer conflict, area control, 4X and any game with open trading.

personas.label: 4X Spreadsheet Admiral
play_goals: wants strategic planning to be rewarded
likely_failure_modes: snowballs past the table
spends five minutes on upkeep maths
breaks_on: upkeep that scales with empire size
tech timing without a fixed window
review_questions: Does their round-3 lead ever close?
How much bookkeeping does their position need by the last round?
personas.sample_quote: If I take this now, I'm two engines ahead by turn six.
personas.use_when: 4X, civ and long-arc economic games; snowball checks.

personas.label: Card Game Grinder
play_goals: wants interactable combos
likely_failure_modes: finds an infinite loop
argues priority with players who don't know the term
breaks_on: triggered abilities with no stack or order
effects that copy or repeat effects
review_questions: Can two cards trigger each other forever?
Who resolves first when both players trigger at once?
personas.sample_quote: In response to that, I play this. Does it fizzle?
personas.use_when: Card-driven, CCG/LCG-style, and anything with reactions or interrupts.

personas.label: Wargame Grognard
play_goals: wants fairness with credible simulation tone
likely_failure_modes: stops the game to argue measurement
plays the simulation, not the rules
red_flags_to_watch: line of sight undefined at edges
breaks_on: line-of-sight with no corner or edge rule
review_questions: Is line of sight defined for the corner cases?
Does any rule produce a historically absurd result?
personas.sample_quote: Base to base or centre to centre? The rules don't say.
personas.use_when: Historical and simulation wargames.

personas.label: Pro Tournament Wargamer
play_goals: wants reproducible outcomes
likely_failure_modes: finds and plays the dominant list
wins on a rule others didn't know
breaks_on: anything a judge would have to interpret
scenarios with an unanswered first-player question
review_questions: What does the win rate look like for whoever goes first?
Is there one list or build that beats everything?
personas.sample_quote: If it's not written down, it's legal.
personas.use_when: Competitive and tournament play, organised play kits, and balance passes.

personas.label: Chess Club Mind
play_goals: wants skill to decide results
likely_failure_modes: disengages when luck decides
treats catch-up rules as charity
breaks_on: hidden information with no deduction path
review_questions: Can a better player reliably win?
Where does randomness override a decision?
personas.sample_quote: So I played better and still lost on a roll?
personas.use_when: Two-player and abstract-adjacent games; any game claiming to be skill-based.

personas.label: Never Reads Rulebooks
play_goals: wants to be carried (quietly)
likely_failure_modes: plays a guessed version of the rules
never learns the exception that matters
breaks_on: rules that exist only in the rulebook, not on components
review_questions: Could the game be played correctly from the components and player aid alone?
Which rule will they never learn?
personas.sample_quote: Just tell me what I can do this turn.
personas.use_when: Always. Most tables have one.

personas.label: Accessibility Advocate
play_goals: wants inclusive design
likely_failure_modes: can't distinguish components under poor light
stalls on dense reference text
review_questions: Does every colour-coded element have a second cue (shape, icon, text)?
Is any game state shown only in artwork?
personas.sample_quote: Is that red or orange? And what does that little icon mean?
personas.use_when: Every game. Pair with P048, P050 and P072 for a full accessibility pass.

personas.label: Co-op Quarterback
play_goals: wants the team to win
likely_failure_modes: plays everyone else's turn
makes the co-op a solo game
review_questions: Can one player make every decision?
What does each player know that others don't?
personas.sample_quote: Okay, here's what everyone should do this round.
personas.use_when: Co-operative and team games.

personas.label: Analysis Paralysis Maximalist
hates_or_struggles: hidden information that makes planning pointless
table_behaviours: asks others to wait 'just a second'
play_goals: wants to find the best move every turn
likely_failure_modes: single turns longer than the rest of the table's combined
other players disengage during their turn
red_flags_to_watch: no way to plan during others' turns
breaks_on: menus with ten or more equally viable actions
decisions that can't be planned until your turn starts
late-game turns that open more options than early ones
review_questions: What's the longest turn they'll take, and when in the game is it?
Can they plan during other players' turns, or does the board change too much?
personas.sample_quote: Sorry, nearly there. Just checking one more option.
personas.use_when: Any game with open action menus or long final rounds; downtime checks.

personas.label: Abstract Purist
table_behaviours: plays the same opening until it's solved
play_goals: wants depth from few rules
likely_failure_modes: dismisses thematic rules as noise and ignores them
solves the opening and gets bored
red_flags_to_watch: exceptions that exist only for theme
review_questions: Which rules could be cut without losing a decision?
Is there a forced or dominant opening?
personas.sample_quote: Why does this need an exception? Make it a general rule.
personas.use_when: Any game claiming elegance or depth; rule-count audits.

personas.label: Meta-Chaser
hates_or_struggles: balance that only exists on paper
play_goals: wants to win with the strongest known line
likely_failure_modes: finds and repeats a dominant strategy until the game feels solved
drags the group's play towards one line
red_flags_to_watch: no counterplay to a known line
breaks_on: static balance with no response options
review_questions: What's the strongest build or faction, and what beats it?
Does the game stay interesting once everyone knows the best line?
personas.sample_quote: Everyone's running this faction now. It's just better.
personas.use_when: Games with factions, decks, builds or expansions; replay-value checks.

personas.label: Speedrunner
play_goals: wants the game to keep moving
likely_failure_modes: skips mandatory upkeep to save time
makes moves before others finish theirs
red_flags_to_watch: optional steps that are secretly important
rules that need a pause to resolve
breaks_on: resolution that needs everyone to stop
review_questions: Which mandatory step will they skip for speed?
Does play order matter enough that doing things simultaneously breaks it?
personas.sample_quote: Done. Next. Whose go is it?
personas.use_when: Fillers and mid-weight games where pace matters; upkeep checks.

personas.label: Salty Loser
table_behaviours: blames dice or rules after losing
play_goals: wants losses to feel fair
likely_failure_modes: disengages once behind
relitigates rulings after the fact
red_flags_to_watch: no path back from an early mistake
losses decided by a single roll
breaks_on: early mistakes that can't be recovered
rules that let the table pile on the loser
review_questions: When does a trailing player realise they can't win, and what do they do next?
Which loss here will feel unfair rather than earned?
personas.sample_quote: That's ridiculous. I never stood a chance.
personas.use_when: Competitive games with snowballs or elimination; pair with design/negative_feedback.md.

personas.label: Deluxe Component Collector
hates_or_struggles: components that don't match the rules
play_goals: wants the game to look and feel finished
likely_failure_modes: plays with mixed-edition components that conflict
spends the evening on setup
red_flags_to_watch: component counts that don't match the rules
deluxe parts with different text from retail
breaks_on: component limits not stated ("are tokens limited?")
review_questions: Are component limits stated, or will people assume they're infinite?
Does setup take longer than the first round?
personas.sample_quote: Hold on, the deluxe version of this card says something different.
personas.use_when: Any game with lots of components or multiple editions; setup and component-limit checks.

personas.label: Campaign Game Master
table_behaviours: runs the campaign for the group
fudges rules to keep the story going
play_goals: wants the campaign to hold together over months
likely_failure_modes: loses campaign state between sessions
fudges a rule and creates a precedent
red_flags_to_watch: choices that can brick the campaign
breaks_on: rules that change mid-campaign without a record
review_questions: Can the game be packed up and resumed three weeks later without arguments?
Can a bad early choice make the campaign unwinnable?
personas.sample_quote: Right, where did we leave off? Who had the relic?
personas.use_when: Campaign, legacy and scenario-based games.

personas.label: Family Game Parent
table_behaviours: bends rules so the youngest can play
play_goals: wants everyone to enjoy it and nobody to cry
likely_failure_modes: simplifies rules in ways that break balance
lets a child win and the game loses its point
review_questions: Can a parent teach this to an eight-year-old in five minutes?
What happens to the game if the youngest player gets help?
personas.sample_quote: Okay, we'll say you can do that because you're new.
personas.use_when: Family and kid-friendly games; anything labelled 8+ or 10+.

personas.label: Child Player, Age 8–10
table_behaviours: wants to move pieces even when it's not their turn
play_goals: wants to have fun and feel clever
likely_failure_modes: loses track of their own goal
takes moves that look exciting over moves that help
red_flags_to_watch: rules that need reading during play
review_questions: Does anything happen for them during other players' turns?
Can they play from pictures alone?
personas.sample_quote: Is it my turn yet? Can I roll?
personas.use_when: Any game marketed to families or children.

personas.label: Competitive Teen
table_behaviours: looks for exploits like a video game glitch
argues with siblings or friends over rules
play_goals: wants to beat everyone
likely_failure_modes: abuses loopholes as 'speedrun tech'
targets the weakest player
breaks_on: loopholes in movement or action limits
review_questions: What loophole would they find and use every turn?
Do they have fun before the game gets going?
personas.sample_quote: Wait, so if I do this, it's infinite? Sick.
personas.use_when: Light-to-mid competitive games aimed at younger audiences; exploit hunts.

personas.label: Club Night Historical Wargamer
hates_or_struggles: rules density causing delays between rounds
play_goals: wants speed
wants clarity
wants to finish within one club evening
likely_failure_modes: game unfinished by closing time
end-of-round rule lookups eat the evening
red_flags_to_watch: end-of-round phases that need the rulebook
scenario length longer than a club slot
review_questions: Can a scenario finish in a three-hour club slot, including setup?
How many rulebook lookups happen between rounds?
personas.sample_quote: We've got forty minutes left. Can we finish this round?
personas.use_when: Wargames played at clubs or in time-boxed sessions.

personas.label: Overconfident Newbie
table_behaviours: says 'got it' before the teach ends
play_goals: wants to look like they know what they're doing
likely_failure_modes: plays an invented rule with total confidence
doesn't ask, so mistakes go unnoticed
red_flags_to_watch: rules where the intuitive reading is wrong
no visible check that a move was legal
breaks_on: terms that sound like their everyday meaning but aren't
legality that can't be checked at a glance
review_questions: Where does the intuitive reading differ from the actual rule?
Will an illegal move be obvious to the rest of the table?
personas.sample_quote: Nah, I've got it. It's basically like Monopoly.
personas.use_when: Any game teaching new players; intuition-trap checks.

personas.label: Solo Rules Auditor
hates_or_struggles: solo modes bolted on as an afterthought
bot decisions that need human judgement
play_goals: wants to play correctly with nobody to ask
likely_failure_modes: stalls with no one to ask
plays the bot wrong and gets a skewed result
red_flags_to_watch: solo rules that refer to multiplayer rules ambiguously
breaks_on: automated opponent rules with unresolved ties
"choose the best option" for a bot
solo setup buried in the multiplayer rules
review_questions: Can the bot's every decision be made without judgement?
Could they play correctly with nobody to ask?
personas.sample_quote: The bot can go left or right. The rules don't say which.
personas.use_when: Any game with a solo mode or automated opponent.

personas.label: Theme-First Immersion Player
play_goals: wants to feel the story
likely_failure_modes: plays what makes sense in the story, not what the rules say
makes weak moves for flavour
red_flags_to_watch: theme implies a rule that doesn't exist
breaks_on: flavour text that sounds like rules text
review_questions: Does the theme suggest a rule that isn't there?
Can flavour text be confused with rules text?
personas.sample_quote: Surely my knight can climb the wall, he's a knight.
personas.use_when: Thematic, adventure and narrative games; flavour/rules separation checks.

personas.label: Streamer Brain
play_goals: wants moments worth clipping
likely_failure_modes: prioritises spectacle over winning, skewing playtest data
hides confusion to look competent
red_flags_to_watch: turns that can't be followed by a viewer
breaks_on: hidden information that's invisible to an audience
review_questions: Can someone watching follow what just happened?
Does the game end on a high or a whimper?
personas.sample_quote: Chat, watch this. This is either genius or a disaster.
personas.use_when: Games with marketing or streaming ambitions; pacing and climax checks.

personas.label: Negotiation Monster
play_goals: wants to win through people
likely_failure_modes: out-talks quieter players
breaks a deal the rules didn't define as binding
red_flags_to_watch: quiet players shut out of decisions
breaks_on: rules that allow promises of future actions
review_questions: What can they promise, and is any of it enforceable?
Can a quiet player still compete with them?
personas.sample_quote: Give me that and I'll owe you one. Trust me.
personas.use_when: Negotiation, trading, political and multiplayer conflict games.

personas.label: Turn-Timer Advocate
table_behaviours: plans their turn early and gets restless
play_goals: wants the game to fit the evening
likely_failure_modes: pushes others into hasty moves
abandons the game when it overruns
red_flags_to_watch: game length varies by more than 50%
breaks_on: end conditions that depend on player choice
review_questions: What's the realistic range of game length?
Can a player stall the end?
personas.sample_quote: Box says 60 minutes. We're at two hours.
personas.use_when: Any game with a stated play time; length-variance checks.

personas.label: Rulebook Skimmer
hates_or_struggles: mechanisms that look standard but aren't
table_behaviours: assumes a mechanism works like another game
play_goals: wants to be playing in five minutes
likely_failure_modes: applies another game's rules to a familiar-looking mechanism
misses the one twist that makes the game different
red_flags_to_watch: familiar mechanism with a non-standard twist
breaks_on: rules missing from headings and diagrams
review_questions: What do they get wrong if they assume it plays like the closest well-known game?
Is every critical rule visible in a heading, diagram or bold text?
personas.sample_quote: It's basically like that other game, right?
personas.use_when: Any game using familiar mechanisms; experienced-player teach checks.

personas.label: Second-Language Reader
play_goals: wants to understand the rules exactly
likely_failure_modes: takes idioms literally
treats synonyms as different rules
red_flags_to_watch: idioms and slang in rules text
breaks_on: idioms and phrasal verbs ("take out", "knock back")
review_questions: Does each game term mean exactly one thing everywhere?
Would a translation app get this sentence right?
personas.sample_quote: Is 'spend' and 'pay' the same thing here?
personas.use_when: Any game shipping internationally or likely to be translated.

personas.label: TTRPG Convert
table_behaviours: expects a GM to rule on edge cases
play_goals: wants freedom of action
likely_failure_modes: tries actions the rules don't allow
expects rulings instead of rules
red_flags_to_watch: no closed list of legal actions
rules that need a GM to interpret
breaks_on: no explicit list of what you can do
review_questions: Is the list of legal actions closed and explicit?
Which edge case would they expect a GM to rule on?
personas.sample_quote: Can I try to sneak past instead?
personas.use_when: Adventure, dungeon-crawl and narrative games.

personas.label: Deckbuilder Optimiser
play_goals: wants an efficient engine
likely_failure_modes: builds a combo that ends the game early
exploits unclear reshuffle timing
breaks_on: cards that draw or replay cards
review_questions: What happens when the draw pile runs out mid-effect?
Can a thin deck combo forever?
personas.sample_quote: Five cards in my deck, and they all chain.
personas.use_when: Deckbuilders, bag-builders and engine games.

personas.label: Lapsed Gamer, Returning
table_behaviours: asks what terms like 'worker placement' mean
compares to games from decades ago
play_goals: wants to get back into the hobby without feeling left behind
likely_failure_modes: misses meanings carried by hobby jargon
plays older-game conventions
review_questions: Which terms assume hobby knowledge?
Is there a glossary or legend for every icon?
personas.sample_quote: In my day you just rolled and moved.
personas.use_when: Gateway and mass-market games; jargon checks.

personas.label: Old Hand, Low Patience
table_behaviours: interrupts the teach to skip ahead
play_goals: wants something new and well-made
likely_failure_modes: checks out after a slow first round
misses new rules by assuming old ones
breaks_on: rules that add complexity without decisions
review_questions: What does this game do that a classic doesn't?
Is the first round interesting?
personas.sample_quote: We've seen this before, and it was better without the extra step.
personas.use_when: Any game pitched at hobby veterans; elegance checks.

personas.label: Convention Demo Drop-In
table_behaviours: forms an opinion in ten minutes
play_goals: wants to know if they'd buy it
likely_failure_modes: judges the game on a half-understood first turn
leaves before the payoff
red_flags_to_watch: game not fun in the first ten minutes
rules needed before the first turn
breaks_on: rules that must be learned before any action
payoff only in the late game
demos that can't be joined mid-game
review_questions: What's fun in the first ten minutes?
Can someone join a demo mid-game?
personas.sample_quote: So what's the hook? What makes this one different?
personas.use_when: Games being demoed at shows or pitched to publishers.

personas.label: The Group's Teacher
table_behaviours: reads the rulebook before game night
play_goals: wants to teach the game in under fifteen minutes
likely_failure_modes: teaches their own misreading to the whole table
omits a rule that seemed minor
red_flags_to_watch: rules that only make sense out of order
breaks_on: rulebooks organised by component instead of by turn
review_questions: What order would they teach this in, and does the rulebook follow it?
Which rule will they forget to mention?
personas.sample_quote: Right, I'll explain the turn first, then we'll come back to scoring.
personas.use_when: Every game; teach-order and rulebook-structure checks.

personas.label: Component Confuser
table_behaviours: places pieces on the wrong track
play_goals: wants to do the right thing without second-guessing
likely_failure_modes: mixes up similar components
puts tokens in the wrong supply
red_flags_to_watch: components that differ only by colour or small print
breaks_on: two token types with similar shapes
review_questions: Which two components could be confused, and what breaks if they are?
Is every board area labelled?
personas.sample_quote: Is this the gold or the coin? They look the same.
personas.use_when: Games with many component types; production and graphic-design checks.

personas.label: Dice Goblin
play_goals: wants big moments from dice
likely_failure_modes: takes reckless risks that swing the game
loses track of reroll limits
breaks_on: modifiers that stack in unclear order
review_questions: What's the swingiest roll in the game, and when does it happen?
Can rerolls stack?
personas.sample_quote: Six dice, need three successes. Let's go!
personas.use_when: Dice-driven games and skirmish combat; variance checks.

personas.label: Legacy Completionist
table_behaviours: won't move on until a rule is clear
play_goals: wants to see everything the game has
likely_failure_modes: makes an irreversible mistake from an unclear instruction
misses content through a misread unlock
breaks_on: no way to undo a mistake
review_questions: What irreversible action could be done wrong?
Is every unlock trigger stated precisely?
personas.sample_quote: Before I put this sticker on: are we sure?
personas.use_when: Legacy and campaign games with permanent changes.

personas.label: Scenario Designer
table_behaviours: reads rules for the intent behind them
play_goals: wants rules robust enough to build on
likely_failure_modes: builds scenarios the rules don't support
exposes assumptions only the base game hides
red_flags_to_watch: rules that only work in base scenarios
hard-coded assumptions about map size or player count
breaks_on: rules that assume a specific setup
player-count specific rules hidden in text
review_questions: Which rules break if the map or player count changes?
Are design assumptions written down?
personas.sample_quote: This only works because the base map has no rivers.
personas.use_when: Games with scenarios, modular boards or expansion plans.

personas.label: Spreadsheet Enjoyer
play_goals: wants evidence the game is balanced
likely_failure_modes: draws conclusions from too few games
optimises towards their own metric
red_flags_to_watch: scoring that can't be audited after the game
review_questions: Could the final score be recounted from the board state?
What would their win-rate spreadsheet show after twenty games?
personas.sample_quote: Faction B has won seven of the last nine.
personas.use_when: Asymmetric and competitive games; balance and scoring audits.

personas.label: Tournament Judge
play_goals: wants rulings to be consistent across tables
likely_failure_modes: has to rule on gaps the designer never considered
inconsistent rulings between events
review_questions: Which rule would a judge have to interpret?
Could two judges rule differently on the same case?
personas.sample_quote: I need a ruling I can apply at every table, not a vibe.
personas.use_when: Competitive and organised-play games; terminology audits.

personas.label: Colour-Blind Player
play_goals: wants to play without asking for help
likely_failure_modes: misidentifies player pieces or card types
makes moves on misread colour information
breaks_on: colour-coded card types with no icon
review_questions: Is any information carried by colour alone?
Can they tell every player colour apart?
personas.sample_quote: Which of these is mine? Red and green look the same to me.
personas.use_when: Every game. Roughly one in twelve men has some colour vision deficiency.

personas.label: Edge-Case Hunter
play_goals: wants the rules to hold up under pressure
likely_failure_modes: derails play with hypotheticals
finds a contradiction that halts the game
breaks_on: rules that contradict each other in edge cases
review_questions: What's the weirdest legal situation they could construct?
Which two rules contradict each other at the edges?
personas.sample_quote: What if I'm adjacent to both and neither moves?
personas.use_when: Every game before release; adversarial rules audits.

personas.label: Low-Vision Player
play_goals: wants independent access to game information
likely_failure_modes: can't read information other players can see
misses changes to shared board state
red_flags_to_watch: important state shown only in small print
breaks_on: information spread across a large board
review_questions: What's the smallest text with gameplay meaning?
Can they track board state without help?
personas.sample_quote: Could you read that card out for me?
personas.use_when: Every game; production and graphic-design checks.

personas.label: Chaos Gremlin
table_behaviours: makes strange moves to see what happens
tests how far the rules stretch
play_goals: wants to cause memorable chaos
likely_failure_modes: kingmakes deliberately
creates game states no one planned for
red_flags_to_watch: moves that wreck the game for others with no gain
review_questions: What happens if someone plays to cause chaos, not to win?
Can one player ruin the game for everyone?
personas.sample_quote: What if I just... do this?
personas.use_when: Multiplayer and party games; robustness against irrational play.

personas.label: Digital Implementation Player
hates_or_struggles: rules the app enforces but the book doesn't explain
table_behaviours: learns the game from an app
relies on the interface to stop illegal moves
play_goals: wants the game to handle the rules
likely_failure_modes: can't play the physical version without the app
doesn't know upkeep the app did silently
red_flags_to_watch: rules the digital version automates silently
breaks_on: upkeep steps automated in digital versions
review_questions: What does the app do automatically that a physical table forgets?
Do the app and rulebook ever disagree?
personas.sample_quote: Oh, I've only played this online. The app does all that.
personas.use_when: Games with digital versions or online play.

personas.label: Quiet Optimiser
play_goals: wants to enjoy solving their own puzzle
likely_failure_modes: silently misplays a rule and never asks
rarely gives feedback unless asked
red_flags_to_watch: confusion that doesn't surface at the table
breaks_on: games where table talk decides outcomes
feedback processes that favour loud players
review_questions: Would they ask for help if they were confused?
Are there rules errors nobody would notice?
personas.sample_quote: (Says nothing, wins by twelve points.)
personas.use_when: Any playtest; silent-error checks and feedback-collection design.

personas.label: Conflict-Averse Peacemaker
table_behaviours: makes suboptimal moves to keep the peace
play_goals: wants everyone to have a good time
likely_failure_modes: refuses to use mechanics that harm others
leaves the leader unchallenged
red_flags_to_watch: games where peace lets the leader win
breaks_on: game balance that assumes players will attack the leader
take-that cards as the main catch-up tool
review_questions: Does the game stay balanced if nobody wants to attack?
Are any attacks mandatory?
personas.sample_quote: Do I have to take it from someone? Can't I just take it from the bank?
personas.use_when: Any game relying on player-driven balance; negative feedback checks.

personas.label: Hidden-Role Liar
table_behaviours: pushes the rules on what can be shown
play_goals: wants to deceive and be believed
likely_failure_modes: exploits information leaks from components or handling
lies about rules as well as roles
red_flags_to_watch: no rule on lying about rules
breaks_on: silence on what can be revealed
review_questions: Can hidden information leak through component handling?
Is lying about rules or public information allowed?
personas.sample_quote: I'm definitely the good guy. Look at my face.
personas.use_when: Social deduction, hidden-role and bluffing games.

personas.label: Boardgame Café Staff
table_behaviours: teaches games to strangers all day
returns to tables to answer questions
play_goals: wants to teach in five minutes and leave the table playing correctly
likely_failure_modes: leaves the table with a shortened teach that misses a rule
teaches the café version, not the real one
breaks_on: rules learned only after the first round
games that can't recover from missing pieces
review_questions: Can the table keep playing correctly after the teacher walks away?
Which rule will the shortened teach miss?
personas.sample_quote: Okay, you've got the basics. I'll check back in twenty minutes.
personas.use_when: Mass-market and café-friendly games; teach-and-leave checks.

personas.label: Miniatures Painter-Hobbyist
hates_or_struggles: rules that need lots of tokens on the table
table_behaviours: plays slowly to enjoy the table
play_goals: wants the table to look great
likely_failure_modes: uses custom models or terrain that change measurements
fields units that look good but play badly
red_flags_to_watch: custom bases or models affecting rules
breaks_on: base size and model height affecting line of sight
terrain categories that depend on appearance
review_questions: What breaks if they use custom models or terrain?
How much token clutter ends up on the table?
personas.sample_quote: I converted this one myself. Does the spear count for reach?
personas.use_when: Miniatures and skirmish wargames.

personas.label: Tired After Work
play_goals: wants to unwind
likely_failure_modes: forgets rules more as the evening goes on
misses late-game triggers
red_flags_to_watch: important rules that only come up late
heavy decisions at the end of the game
breaks_on: decisions needing precise maths when tired
rules that are only used once
review_questions: Which late-game rule will a tired table forget?
Does the game still work if players play on autopilot?
personas.sample_quote: Sorry, my brain's gone. What does this do again?
personas.use_when: Any game played on weeknights; late-game attention checks.

personas.label: Kingmaker By Accident
hates_or_struggles: games where the end feels decided
table_behaviours: makes moves that decide who wins
play_goals: wants to still matter when behind
likely_failure_modes: hands the win to someone else
plays aimlessly once out of contention
red_flags_to_watch: nothing to play for when behind
breaks_on: endgames where trailing players choose the winner
scoring that rewards targeting the leader
review_questions: Who decides the winner when one player can't win?
What does a trailing player play for?
personas.sample_quote: I didn't mean to give you the game. I just took the best move I had.
personas.use_when: Multiplayer games with three or more players; endgame checks.

personas.label: Solo Wargamer vs Bot
play_goals: wants a credible opponent without another person
likely_failure_modes: bot gets stuck in a loop
plays both sides with information the bot shouldn't have
review_questions: Does every flowchart branch end in a legal action?
Can the bot get stuck?
personas.sample_quote: The flowchart says attack the nearest unit. Two are equally near.
personas.use_when: Solo wargames and any game with a bot or automa.

personas.label: Engine-Builder Snowballer
play_goals: wants their engine to explode in the late game
likely_failure_modes: runs away with the game with no counterplay
takes final turns that last ten minutes
breaks_on: late-game turns with dozens of actions
review_questions: What's the biggest possible final turn?
Can anyone slow a runaway engine?
personas.sample_quote: Watch this, it's all going to chain.
personas.use_when: Engine builders and tableau games; snowball and downtime checks.

personas.label: Grumpy Rules Editor
table_behaviours: reads the rulebook with a pen
play_goals: wants the rulebook to be correct and usable
likely_failure_modes: focuses on style over gameplay issues
finds inconsistencies others miss
breaks_on: rules defined in two places differently
review_questions: Is every game term defined exactly once?
Does every cross-reference point to the right place?
personas.sample_quote: You call it 'Action' on page 3 and 'action' on page 7. Same thing?
personas.use_when: Every rulebook before print; editorial audits.

personas.label: Luck-Loving Casual
play_goals: wants a fair chance to win regardless of skill
likely_failure_modes: takes reckless risks
disengages from heavy decisions
red_flags_to_watch: skill gaps too wide for luck to bridge
planning phases with no luck element
review_questions: Can a newer player still win sometimes?
Is there enough uncertainty to keep it fun?
personas.sample_quote: Ooh, let's see what happens!
personas.use_when: Family and light games; skill-gap checks.

personas.label: Forum Rules Checker
play_goals: wants the official answer
likely_failure_modes: brings conflicting unofficial rulings
halts play to look things up
red_flags_to_watch: frequently asked questions not in the rulebook
breaks_on: ambiguities that need the designer's intent
review_questions: Which rule will generate the most forum questions?
Is the answer to every likely question in the rulebook?
personas.sample_quote: There's a designer ruling on this, hang on.
personas.use_when: Any game pre-release; FAQ-prevention checks.

personas.label: Distracted Phone Checker
likes: games that don't need constant attention
play_goals: wants to socialise and play at the same time
likely_failure_modes: misses changes to board state
takes turns based on outdated information
red_flags_to_watch: state changes during other players' turns
important info only announced, not shown
breaks_on: state changes that aren't visible on the board
review_questions: If they look away for a turn, can they catch up from the board?
What happens during other players' turns that affects them?
personas.sample_quote: Sorry, what did I miss?
personas.use_when: Every game; board-state legibility and downtime checks.

personas.label: Wargame Umpire
hates_or_struggles: rules that leave nothing for the umpire
play_goals: wants credible outcomes with hidden information
likely_failure_modes: makes rulings that players dispute
workload grows with player count
breaks_on: rules needing umpire judgement without guidance
review_questions: What does the umpire need to decide, and is there guidance?
How does umpire workload scale with players?
personas.sample_quote: As umpire, I'll rule that. But the rules should have said.
personas.use_when: Refereed wargames, hidden-movement and fog-of-war games.

personas.label: Rules-as-Written Literalist
play_goals: wants the rules to say exactly what they mean
likely_failure_modes: applies literal readings that break the game
won't accept intent-based rulings
red_flags_to_watch: rules whose literal reading differs from intent
review_questions: What does the literal reading say, and does it match the intent?
Is every "it" or "they" unambiguous?
personas.sample_quote: It says 'a unit', not 'each unit'. So only one.
personas.use_when: Every game; wording audits.

personas.label: Iconography Reader
play_goals: wants to read the game at a glance
likely_failure_modes: misreads an icon that changes meaning
ignores text that modifies the icon
breaks_on: icons that mean different things in different places
review_questions: Does every icon mean one thing everywhere?
Does any card text contradict its icons?
personas.sample_quote: The arrow icon means move, right? Even here?
personas.use_when: Icon-heavy games; graphic-design checks.

personas.label: Player-Aid Dependent
table_behaviours: plays entirely from the reference card
play_goals: wants everything they need on one card
likely_failure_modes: follows an incomplete aid
misses rules that aren't on the aid
red_flags_to_watch: key rules missing from the aid
review_questions: Does the player aid match the rulebook exactly?
What will they miss if they only use the aid?
personas.sample_quote: It's not on the card, so I didn't do it.
personas.use_when: Any game with a player aid or reference card.

personas.label: Late Arrival
play_goals: wants to join in without slowing everyone down
likely_failure_modes: misses setup-dependent rules
plays catch-up with an incomplete teach
breaks_on: rules taught only at the start
board state that needs history to read
review_questions: Could someone join after round one?
Which rules only get mentioned during setup?
personas.sample_quote: Sorry I'm late! What did I miss?
personas.use_when: Social and casual games; mid-game legibility checks.

personas.label: Print-and-Play Prototyper
play_goals: wants to help shape the design
likely_failure_modes: plays an outdated rules version
mistakes prototype placeholders for final components
review_questions: Is there a version number and changelog?
Do placeholder components carry any gameplay meaning?
personas.sample_quote: Which version of the rules is this? The card says something different.
personas.use_when: Prototype playtests; version control and feedback-loop checks.

personas.label: Dyslexic Player
play_goals: wants to play without reading barriers
likely_failure_modes: misreads similar-looking words ("gain" vs "game", "draw" vs "draft")
slows down on text-heavy turns
review_questions: How much reading does a turn need?
Are any game terms easily confused visually?
personas.sample_quote: Could you read that one? The font's a bit much.
personas.use_when: Every game; text-load and typography checks.
